question.text: Ms. Ananya Deshpande is structuring an Indian Category II AIF and wants to set a USD-equivalent gross return hurdle for overseas LPs. Indian real risk-free rate is estimated at 3%, expected inflation is 5.5%, and the manager adds a 7% risk premium for illiquid private credit exposure. Using the Fisher-style nominal return formula from NISM Ch 1, what is the approximate required NOMINAL rate of return (before risk premium) and the TOTAL required rate of return?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 1.4.1, NRR = [(1 + Real) x (1 + Inflation)] - 1 = (1.03 x 1.055) - 1 = 1.08665 - 1 = 8.665%, which rounds to 8.67%. Adding the 7% risk premium gives a total required return of 15.665%, which rounds to 15.67%. The multiplicative form captures the compounding cross-term (0.03 x 0.055 = 0.165%) that the simple additive form misses. The Trap: Option A is the naive linear approximation (Real + Inflation), which under-states the nominal rate in inflationary environments. Option B drops both the cross-term and rounds down further. Option C rounds 8.665% downward instead of to the nearest hundredth. Note: Apply the multiplicative Fisher form and round 8.665% to 8.67%, then add the 7% risk premium to get 15.67%.
